items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: one of the first trumpet players to leave from New Orleans along with King Oliver and the other guys.

ctx.x: What's your name? Well, sure, Paul. I'll be happy to. My name is Don Albert, professionally, and my family name is Dominique. I imagine you know of my uncle in Chicago. He still uses his name Dominique. His name is Natty Dominique, one of the first trumpet players to leave from New Orleans along with King Oliver and the other guys. And after this, where you are now, we're in San Antonio, Texas. This is my residence, and it's 715 St. James. Been living here for the last five years in this home. We bought this…
This is June the 6th, 1961, and I'm Paul Crawford. You were talking about this fellow, one of the first guys you took, you know, when you left New Orleans? No. A banjo player or something?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: And that's where Bonnie and Alvin Nicholas left and went up to Chicago to join. King Oliver.

ctx.x: Could he play fast or did he? Play anything.

He's played old Tom Anderson's cafe up here where Cress is up on. Yeah. And that was days when Bonnie was with a real young fella, Paul Byrd, and they had a tremendous little band there. And that's where Bonnie and Alvin Nicholas left and went up to Chicago to join. King Oliver.

Well, it strikes me, you know, when I talk to New Orleans musicians, I never know exactly when they say somebody's great, exactly what the man was great at. Some guys are great at, say, you take Caffrey Dyer and Jerry. I don't know if he was great at keeping a beat with the correct chord changes.
